draft.headline: Chronic absence (21%) is the biggest flag, and 23 students are flagged for both absence and academics, so one shared plan could reach them.

bigPicture.label: chronically absent in Q1
bigPicture.point: Attendance is the largest flag, well above the 12% flagged for academics.
bigPicture.read: Is missed time spread across the day or tied to certain periods? Period-by-period attendance records would show it.
bigPicture.do: Pull period-by-period attendance for flagged students and review it at the next leadership meeting.

bigPicture.label: flagged in both attendance and academics
bigPicture.point: Most of the 36 students flagged for academics are also chronically absent.
bigPicture.read: Attendance and academic flags travel together, so one plan can meet both needs.
bigPicture.do: Build one shared plan for these students and review progress after a 6-week cycle.
bigPicture.doLess: Running separate attendance and academic referrals for the same students.

bigPicture.label: grade 12 chronically absent
bigPicture.point: Grades 12 and 9 (26%) sit above the 21% school-wide rate; grade 11 has fewer than 10.
bigPicture.read: What is different for grades 9 and 12? Compare their schedules and period-by-period attendance with grade 11.
bigPicture.do: Start with grades 9 and 12 when placing attendance supports this quarter.
bigPicture.doLess: Spreading attendance supports evenly across all four grades.

counselor.label: tier 3, flagged in both areas
counselor.point: This is 8% of students, the group with the most flags.
counselor.do: Run a 6-week check-in group pairing attendance goals with course-recovery goals for these students.

counselor.label: grade 9 chronically absent
counselor.point: Higher than the 21% school-wide rate, early in high school.
counselor.do: Offer a 4-week attendance check-in group to flagged grade 9 students.
counselor.doLess: Whole-grade attendance lessons that reach students who are already attending.

administrator.label: chronically absent, the largest flag
administrator.point: Attendance flags are close to double the 12% flagged for academics.
administrator.read: Do absences cluster in particular periods or schedule blocks? Period-by-period attendance would tell.
administrator.do: Review the master schedule against period-level absence for grades 9 and 12 this quarter.
administrator.doLess: School-wide attendance announcements aimed at everyone.

administrator.label: in tier 2
administrator.point: Tier 2 is the larger support group, more than double tier 3 at 8%.
administrator.do: Protect a weekly intervention block for tier 2 students for the next 6 weeks.

teachers.label: flagged for academics
teachers.point: Lower than attendance at 21%, yet many of these students are also chronically absent.
teachers.read: Missed class time and failing grades appear together, so make-up work may matter as much as reteaching.
teachers.do: Give returning students a written make-up plan on their first day back.
teachers.doLess: Late penalties on work missed during absences.

teachers.label: grade 9 flagged for academics
teachers.point: Highest academic rate among grades with shown counts; grade 12 is 14%.
teachers.do: Use a brief greeting and task check at the door in grade 9 classes for 4 weeks.

supportTeam.label: tier 3, flagged in both areas
supportTeam.point: These students need coordinated tier 3 support rather than two separate tracks.
supportTeam.do: Make one shared list of these students and review it every 2 weeks.
supportTeam.doLess: Separate attendance and academic case reviews for the same students.

supportTeam.label: chronically absent students
supportTeam.point: This is the largest flagged group, ahead of 36 flagged for academics.
supportTeam.read: What gets in the way of attending? Family conversations and attendance staff notes could tell you.
supportTeam.do: Have attendance staff call families of flagged grade 9 and 12 students within 3 weeks, asking what would help.
supportTeam.doLess: Form letters as the only outreach.

connections.label: students flagged in both areas
connections.point: One shared list and one plan keep these students from being handled three separate ways.

steps.step: Share the list of students flagged in both areas and set the review schedule.
Lead a 6-week group for them and report progress at each review.
Send the team a short note when a listed student misses work or class.

connections.label: chronically absent
connections.point: Period-level data lets each role aim its support at the same grades and times.

steps.step: Provide period-by-period attendance for grades 9 and 12 to the intervention team.
Pick the periods with the most missed time and plan family outreach around them.
Schedule check-in groups outside those periods so students do not miss more class.

goals.statement: By [date], students flagged for chronic absence will decrease the chronic absence rate from 21% to [target set by counselor].
By [date], students in grades 9 through 12 will decrease the share flagged for academics from 12% to [target set by counselor].
By [date], students in tier 3 will decrease their share of the school from 8% to [target set by counselor].
goals.baseline: Q1 share of students in tier 3.

draft.limits: Behavior is not in the files, so it was not checked. There is no earlier snapshot, so nothing is compared. Some grade counts are fewer than 10 or not shown. Causes and individual students are not visible.
